intro: Butchers work with sharp tools, serve customers and keep a fast pace. The closest of the 25 careers below is restaurant cooking, with an 89% skill match, but the pay moves are in kitchen leadership: Food Service Managers earn a BLS May 2025 median of $69,390, or 73% more.
why_it_works: A shift at the meat counter means cutting to order, advising customers and keeping the case stocked and safe. O*NET rates social perceptiveness, time management and service orientation at 3 out of 5 for butchers. Cooking and food preparation use the same knife and timing skills. Almost all matches need no extra schooling. The gaps are managing people and money.
tips: Chefs and Head Cooks earn $62,470, which is 56% more, often after a culinary certificate.
Ask to run the department; supervising staff is your most common skill gap.
Animal Breeders earn $51,130, or 27% more, if you want to work with livestock.

faq.q: What jobs can former butchers do?
faq.a: The closest matches are restaurant cooks (89%), Food Preparation Workers (87%) and institution and cafeteria cooks (85%), based on O*NET 31.0. Short order cooks are 84% matched and earn $35,880, which is 11% less than the $40,140 butcher median, so lateral kitchen moves rarely pay more.

faq.q: Which careers for butchers pay more?
faq.a: 6 of the 25 matches pay more. Food Service Managers earn $69,390 (73% more), Chefs and Head Cooks $62,470 (56% more) and Animal Breeders $51,130 (27% more), according to BLS May 2025 data. Head cook roles often expect a certificate or associate program.

faq.q: Do butchers need more education to switch?
faq.a: Rarely. 23 of the 25 matches need no more education than butchers and meat cutters already have, including 9 of the top 10. In the closest match, 47% of workers have a high school diploma or the equivalent, so kitchen experience counts more than formal schooling.

The skills that most often need work are coordination, managing financial resources, managing people and operation and control. Service orientation already rates 3 out of 5 for butchers in O*NET, so learning to run a team and a budget is the main path to higher pay.
